task.name: Routing selects models without checking whether the active account can call them
task.story_text:
## Why

Routing picks a model from the configured pool on price, tier and capability. It
does not ask whether the account the run will dispatch with is permitted to call
that model, so a model the provider has withdrawn stays selectable until a story
dispatches to it and is refused.

That happened on 2026-09-04. OpenAI withdrew `gpt-5.4` from Codex under
ChatGPT-account authentication on 2026-08-31. Routing selected it for dev in two
repositories eight minutes apart; both were refused in five seconds with
`HTTP 400 — The 'gpt-5.4' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT
account`, after WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan had already run and been
paid for. Four stories produced nothing.

Forge already declines to route a model recorded as withdrawn: a `status:
retired` catalog entry carries `dev_capable=False` and empty
`phase_eligibility`, and naming it in `forge.yaml` fails at load with the reason.
Two DeepSeek entries work exactly that way today. The record driving it is
hand-maintained, so the guard fires only for withdrawals a human already found.

A static record is also not sufficient here, and this is what distinguishes this
issue from marking one more entry retired. Availability is a property of the
model *and the credentials in use*: `gpt-5.4` remains callable through Codex
under API-key authentication and is refused only under ChatGPT-account
authentication. No fixed per-identifier status can express that, because the
answer differs by how the run authenticates.

The information needed is already available locally and free. The Codex package
forge pins answers `debug models` from the signed-in account's own catalog with
no generative call, and that catalog does not list `gpt-5.4`. Forge also already
knows it does not know: `check-config` reports `never checked against the
provider's published model list` for every OpenAI profile configured on the
machine, including the ones dev now routes to.

Scope note: this issue is the routing behavior only — which models are eligible,
and withholding one the provider has refused. The readiness *report* that calls
launcher presence "ready" is fuzzypete/theforge#2909. Classifying a refused call's cost as zero
rather than unknown is fuzzypete/theforge#2913.

## Acceptance criteria

Every configured model resolves to exactly one of three states, and the states
are not interchangeable:

- **available** — the account's own list of invocable models includes it. It
  routes normally.
- **unavailable** — that list exists and does not include it. It is logged and
  excluded from selection; routing proceeds with the remaining models.
- **unverified** — no list could be obtained for that provider, or the attempt
  to obtain one failed. **It remains fully eligible for routing**, and the run
  warns once that its availability is unconfirmed. Unverified is never treated
  as unavailable: a provider that publishes no catalog must keep working exactly
  as it does today, and a network failure or an expired login must never disable
  a provider that was serving traffic a minute earlier.

Beyond the three states:

- Availability is resolved for the account and authentication mode the run will
  dispatch with. The same identifier may be available under one auth mode and
  unavailable under another, so nothing records availability as a fixed property
  of the identifier.
- A phase left with no available or unverified model stops the run before any
  spend, naming which models were excluded and why.
- Resolution completes without dispatching a generative request and without the
  operator running anything.
- When a dispatch is nonetheless refused for a reason that is a property of the
  configuration rather than the request — the account may not call this model —
  that model is quarantined for the remainder of the run. No later story, phase
  or role routes to it, and the run continues on the remaining models rather than
  meeting the identical refusal once per story. This applies to an unverified
  model as much as to one the list claimed was available: an explicit refusal is
  stronger evidence than any prior state, and it is what converts unverified into
  unavailable for the rest of that run.
- Entries already marked withdrawn by hand in the packaged catalog remain
  non-routable. Both sources converge on the same outcome; neither overrides the
  other toward availability.
- An availability answer carries the time it was obtained, and one older than the
  existing identity-verification window is refreshed or reported as stale rather
  than reused as current.

## Example

Today, `gpt-5.4` withdrawn upstream and still in the pool:

```
$ forge check-config
    openai/gpt-5.4/cli              never checked against the provider's published model list
  openai-gpt-5.4-cli    openai    cli:codex gpt-5.4     budget=$2.00  ✓ ready

$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4  iter=1
  [DEV] FAIL | exit=1 | cost=unknown
  error output: {"status":400,"error":{"message":"The 'gpt-5.4' model is not
  supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
  ✗ ESCALATE   Dev agent failed and produced no commits ahead of base
```

Wanted:

```
$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded — not available to this account under
             codex ChatGPT-account auth (account catalog, checked 2026-09-05)
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4-mini  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.42  4m 11s
```

And where nothing remains:

```
$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ✗ ROUTING  no model available for phase dev: openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded
             (not available to this account), openai/gpt-5.5/cli excluded
             (not available to this account). Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent.
```

- [P1] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1(d) and the stated provider-wording risk still recognize configuration-property refusals through a small signature table seeded only with the Codex wording, plus runner_codex.PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE. Other provider adapters do not emit that Codex-specific code, and an unmatched account/model-access refusal is only logged. The same identity can therefore be dispatched again on later stories, directly violating the provider-generic quarantine criterion.
  Suggestion: Define a provider-neutral structured account/model-access refusal code at the adapter boundary, or enumerate every supported provider's structured refusal mapping and test each one. Ambiguous 400/request errors should continue to fail open.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan's re-exec risk is carried, not mitigated: it explicitly says os.execv discards the quarantine and may cause one repeated refusal. The current sprint code treats re-exec as continuation of the same sprint, preserving its sprint identity, costs, outcomes, and live work. Losing an exclusion there violates 'for the remainder of the run' and allows a later story in the same sprint to redispatch the refused model.
  Suggestion: Persist the sprint-scoped quarantine evidence before re-exec and restore it using the preserved sprint/run identity, clearing it only when the actual sprint invocation ends. Add a refusal-before-re-exec/later-story-after-re-exec test.
- [P1] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 registers every attempt inside runners/api.py::run_api_agent but never checks quarantine before each _run_single_api_model iteration. The run_agent guard sees only the profile's primary identity, so a preference-list fallback quarantined by an earlier story can still be dispatched when the current primary fails. Conversely, guarding a quarantined primary at run_agent prevents a still-eligible fallback in that preference list from running.
  Suggestion: Consult quarantine on each current_profile before _run_single_api_model, skip quarantined preference entries, and dispatch the next eligible model. Return a routing-exclusion result only when every preference entry is unavailable. Test both a quarantined fallback and a quarantined primary with an eligible fallback.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 5's dispatchable_profile helper filters unavailable candidates but does not emit once-per-run unverified warnings. coordinator/preflight.py::_story_announcements only inventories phase_candidate_profiles and agents, so a distinct knowledge-summary API profile is omitted; state=None pre-story callers likewise bypass the existing warning emission.
  Suggestion: Have the shared fixed-role helper feed every examined candidate through announcements and AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS using the active run token, and test a unique unverified knowledge-summary identity plus an unverified pre-story intake identity.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 6 promises audit evidence for matched and unmatched refusals, but Step 1(b)'s ModelQuarantine stores only excluding entries and Step 2 records only matched signals. MODEL_QUARANTINE.snapshot(token) therefore cannot contain unmatched observations.
  Suggestion: Maintain a separate per-token observation ledger containing both matched and unmatched attempts, with an explicit quarantined flag; overlay only matched entries and audit both. Include profile, model, transport, and bounded provider text for unmatched observations.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The backstop introduces failure_code=model_unavailable_quarantined without modifying coordinator/agent_failure.py. It therefore falls through classify_failure_category as a generic process failure, rather than being explicitly treated as a no-judgment routing exclusion, and the plan has no capability/profile-history attribution test.
  Suggestion: Add coordinator/agent_failure.py to the implementation, explicitly classify the code as a non-judgment routing exclusion, and test that a backstop hit writes nothing to capability or adaptive profile history.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 6 changes the generated coordinator audit shape but omits the mandatory record-schema work enforced by tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py. CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION is owned by coordinator/audit_storage.py and currently has a v50 migration chain and audit_record_schema_v50.json fixture; adding a field without the next migration and fixture predictably fails the gate.
  Suggestion: Add coordinator/audit_storage.py, tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py, and tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v51.json to Steps 6-7; bump the record version and add _migrate_v50_to_v51 plus its MIGRATION_HELPERS entry.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 7 provides end-to-end exclusion checks but still lacks the previously requested direct equality assertion between attempt_dispatch_key and profile_dispatch_key. Because the attempt side is config-free while the availability side applies transport fallback normalization, a mismatch would otherwise be diagnosed only through a larger routing failure.
  Suggestion: Add direct key-equality tests for a plain CLI profile and for an API fallback identity.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 6 does not explicitly document that the first live provider refusal is expected to occur once before quarantine exists, despite the earlier review requesting that operator-facing clarification.
  Suggestion: State in the runbook subsection that one pre-generation refusal may occur per run, is recorded at $0.00 when established, and is the evidence that activates quarantine.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 6 adds a field to the generated run audit, but no step touches the audit record schema machinery. tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py:347 pins the field set against tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v<N>.json and CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 50, audit_storage.py:177, re-exported via audit_substrate.py), with MIGRATION_HELPERS required to satisfy max(MIGRATION_HELPERS) == CURRENT - 1 (audit_storage.py:2907). As written the change fails that guard.
  Suggestion: Add the version bump, the MIGRATION_HELPERS entry and the new fixture to Step 6/7 — the guard's own failure message (test_audit_schema_guard.py:394-403) enumerates the exact four steps.

  Suggestion: Give each token partition a second observation list holding matched and unmatched refusals (overlay applies only to matched), and snapshot both in Step 6 — or narrow the Step 6 claim to matched signals.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's backstop returns failure_code 'model_unavailable_quarantined', but coordinator/agent_failure.py is in no step's file list, so the code is unknown to _TRANSPORT_FAILURE_CODES (line 160), _MODEL_EXECUTION_FAILURE_CODES (line 164) and classify_failure_category (line 329) and falls through to generic failure classification — a backstop hit could be attributed against capability history rather than read as a routing exclusion.
  Suggestion: Classify the new code explicitly in agent_failure.py and assert in Step 7 that a backstopped non-dispatch writes nothing to capability or adaptive profile history.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 derives coordinator-entry tokens from run_warning_key(state), which returns None when neither sprint_name nor run_id is known (model_availability.py:757-768), and Step 1(a) makes a None token fully inert — a standalone forge run without a run_id gets no quarantine at all.
  Suggestion: Mint a local per-run token (uuid4) at the coordinator entry when run_warning_key returns None, reserving None for callers that never enter a run scope.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 says _select_advisor_profile (escalation_advisor_flow.py:108) narrows by the overlaid answer, but it is also called from coordinator/triage_proposal_flow.py:651, which is in no step's file list. If the dev changes its signature to take state or config+state, that caller breaks.
  Suggestion: Keep _select_advisor_profile's signature as-is and have it read the overlaid answer through the state-optional helper (resolve_story_availability + overlay under the ambient token), or add triage_proposal_flow.py to the file list.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The once-per-run unverified warning is emitted from the announcement inventory (_story_announcements over phase candidates and agents), which need not include a distinct fixed-role identity such as the API-transport summary profile (_project_summary_api_profile, knowledge_summary_flow.py:328). Step 5 describes logging exclusions only, so a unique unverified fixed-role identity can dispatch without the required warning.
  Suggestion: Have role_availability.dispatchable_profile emit AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS for every candidate it examines, or extend the announcement inventory to cover fixed-role dispatch identities; test a unique unverified summary profile.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Keys recorded by the config-free attempt_dispatch_key (Step 1c) must equal the keys the overlay compares against, which come from profile_dispatch_key → _apply_transport_fallback → availability_target → dispatch_key (model_availability.py:263-276). A composition mismatch makes the quarantine a silent no-op, and Step 7's exclusion assertions would not localize it.
  Suggestion: Add a direct unit assertion that the key recorded from a refused plain-CLI dispatch equals profile_dispatch_key(profile, config) for that profile, alongside the api_fallback case.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk: only the Codex ChatGPT-account wording is concretely enumerated, and the second rule keys on runner_codex.PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE, which no other runner sets — so another provider's account/model-access refusal initially takes the unmatched path and repeats per story. The design fails open and makes each miss visible, but trigger coverage starts effectively Codex-only.
  Suggestion: Keep the signature table data-driven so a new wording is a one-line addition, and make the unmatched log line carry the dispatched profile, model and enough raw provider text to write that line from run output alone.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk: an ADR-0003 re-exec (docs/adr/0003, sprint a27d1367454a) restarts the process and discards the partition, so evidence gathered before the re-exec is lost and one refusal can repeat afterwards.
  Suggestion: None required — that is today's behaviour; note it in the Step 6 runbook subsection so an operator reading a post-re-exec repeat does not read it as a defect.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] An identity the catalog calls available or unverified still pays one pre-generation refusal per run before registration takes effect — $0.00, then blocked for the remainder.
  Suggestion: State this in the Step 6 runbook subsection so the single refusal reads as expected behaviour.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Third consecutive review flagging this: Step 2's backstop returns failure_code 'model_unavailable_quarantined', and coordinator/agent_failure.py is still in no step's file list — the code stays unknown to _TRANSPORT_FAILURE_CODES (line 160), _MODEL_EXECUTION_FAILURE_CODES (line 164) and classify_failure_category (line 327), so a backstop hit falls to generic failure classification and can be attributed against capability history instead of read as a routing exclusion.
  Suggestion: Add the code to the appropriate frozenset in agent_failure.py and assert in Step 7 that a backstopped non-dispatch records nothing against capability/profile history.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 6 adds a quarantine field to the run audit, but the repo's audit schema is guarded: tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py (line 397 names the required steps) enforces a CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in coordinator/audit_substrate.py plus a new schema fixture whenever the generated audit shape changes — neither audit_substrate.py nor the schema-guard test appears in Steps 6/7, so the plan's audit change will fail that guard as written.
  Suggestion: Add coordinator/audit_substrate.py, tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py, and the next audit_record_schema fixture to Steps 6/7.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Third consecutive review flagging this: Step 6 still claims the audit snapshot shows 'that a refusal went unmatched', but Step 1(b)'s ModelQuarantine holds only quarantined dispatch keys and Step 2 only logs unmatched refusals — MODEL_QUARANTINE.snapshot(token) cannot produce unmatched-refusal evidence, so the provider-wording mitigation's audit trail does not exist as specified.
  Suggestion: Give each token partition a non-excluding observation list recording matched and unmatched refusal signals (overlay applies only to matched), and snapshot both in Step 6 — or scope Step 6's claim to matched signals with unmatched visible in the log only.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Carried plan Risk 3: only the Codex ChatGPT-account refusal signature is concretely enumerated (plus PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE with model-string corroboration), so account/model-access refusals from other providers initially take the unmatched path and fall open to today's per-story repeat — the quarantine AC is provider-generic but trigger recognition starts effectively Codex-only. Visible-by-design (unmatched outcome with raw reason) and fail-open, but coverage grows only as signatures are added.
  Suggestion: Keep the signature table data-driven so a new wording is a one-line addition, and make the unmatched log line carry the dispatched profile, model, and enough raw provider text to write the new signature from run output alone.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 3 derives the coordinator-entry token from run_warning_key(state), which returns None when neither sprint_name nor run_id is set (model_availability.py:757-770), and Step 1(a) makes a None token fully inert — a standalone run whose state lacks both identifiers gets no quarantine at all, so the remainder-of-run clause silently would not apply to it.
  Suggestion: At each run entry, fall back to a locally minted per-run token when run_warning_key returns None, keeping None reserved for callers that never enter a run scope; one test for the no-identifier state.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 7's attempt-seam tests assert exclusion end-to-end but still omit the direct key-equality assertion from two prior reviews: attempt_dispatch_key is config-free while overlay keys come from profile_dispatch_key via _apply_transport_fallback and availability_target (model_availability.py:263-276), so a composition mismatch would surface only as a harder-to-localize exclusion-test failure.
  Suggestion: Add one unit assertion that the key recorded from a refused plain-CLI dispatch equals profile_dispatch_key(profile, config), and that a refused api_fallback's key equals the key of a configured profile naming that API identity.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 5's dispatchable_profile logs unavailable exclusions but does not say it emits the once-per-run unverified warning for fixed-role candidates the routed path never announces (e.g. a distinct knowledge-summary API profile), so a unique unverified fixed-role identity can dispatch without the warning the AC describes for routed models.
  Suggestion: Have the helper route its examined candidates through AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS so fixed-role identities warn once per run like routed ones; one test with a unique unverified summary profile.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] A catalog-available identity that is in fact refused still pays one $0.00 pre-generation refusal per invocation before registration takes effect — bounded, then blocked for the rest of the run.
  Suggestion: Note this in Step 6's runbook subsection so the operator reads the single refusal as expected behaviour rather than a gap.

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach:
Everything in the acceptance criteria except the live-refusal quarantine shipped under #2950 (three states, per-account/auth-mode dispatch identities, no-available-model stop, non-generative resolution, retired-catalog convergence, timestamped answers — docs/guides/controller-runbook.md:92-208). This plan adds the missing clause: an explicit provider refusal converts an identity to unavailable for the rest of the run, and every dispatch site — routed, fixed-role, or pre-story — consults that answer.
Four corrections to the prior attempts, each answering a recurring P1.
(1) REGISTRATION IS PER ATTEMPT, NOT PER RETURNED RESULT. run_agent's return value is not the set of attempts: runners/cli.py::_maybe_run_api_fallback consumes a refused CLI result and may return a later successful API result, and runners/api.py::run_api_agent's preference loop (line 1184) discards every failed model before the one that succeeds. So classification happens where a concrete single-model attempt result exists — beside each `_run_*` CLI call in run_agent, and inside run_api_agent's per-model loop on `current_profile`. Every attempt is classified before any fallback loop advances, so a refused primary followed by a successful fallback quarantines the primary and leaves the fallback eligible.
(2) THE QUARANTINE IS PARTITIONED BY AN EXPLICIT RUN TOKEN, carried ambiently in a contextvars.ContextVar rather than threaded through signatures. reset()-with-one-active-key is abandoned: interleaved runs corrupted it and run_agent had no run identity to attribute a refusal to. No signature in engine.py/sprint/cli changes, so cli/*, eval/preflight_harness.py and every other external caller keep working — and, absent a token, the quarantine is inert in both directions, so a standalone runner invocation after a completed sprint inherits nothing.
(3) THE TOKEN IS ESTABLISHED AT THE OUTERMOST RUN-OWNING BOUNDARY AND INHERITED INWARD. The prior attempt scoped only the coordinator entries and per-story submission, which left every sprint-owned dispatch that happens *before* the first story outside the scope — concretely the two intake-remediation passes, which spend real money on agent rewrites: sprint/runner.py:6464 (in-run, ahead of batch preflight) and cli/sprint.py:1419 → entry_intake.remediate_entry_skipped_issues (entry-skipped, ahead of run_sprint). Both reach run_agent through _build_intake_agent_caller (runner.py:264), so step 2 already classifies their attempts; what they lacked was a token, so a refusal there was dropped and every later story met it again. Deriving a token separately at each site would not fix it either — the entry-skipped pass has only `gate_run_id`, which is not the sprint's later `resolved.name`, so the two halves of one invocation would land in different partitions. So `run_scope` INHERITS: entering it while a token is already active reuses the active token instead of opening a second partition. The CLI sprint invocation opens the scope once, around entry intake and run_sprint together; run_sprint, the coordinator entries and each story worker all inherit it. One `forge sprint` invocation is one partition, end to end.
(4) FIXED-ROLE SELECTORS CONSUME THE AVAILABILITY ANSWER. A generic run_agent guard can only fail a dispatch; it cannot choose the remaining model, which is what the criteria require. The six sites that select a profile from configuration rather than from routing — decomposition assessment, escalation advisor, knowledge summary, landing merge-conflict resolution, and both intake-remediation passes — each filter their own candidates through one shared helper before dispatching, exactly as preflight_flow._availability_checked_preflight_profile already does. The run_agent guard remains, demoted to a last-resort backstop.
Routing-side consumption is unchanged from the prior plan: an overlay on the #2950 answer at story_availability_for and the post-plan checkpoint, so exclusion, pinned-pool member drop, the stop path, warnings and audit all reuse shipped machinery.

steps.description: Run-token-partitioned quarantine, inheriting run_scope, attempt-identity key, refusal predicate, shared selector
steps.details:
Five additions beside the existing availability code.
(a) RUN TOKEN AND INHERITING SCOPE. `RUN_TOKEN: ContextVar[str | None]`, plus `current_run_token()` and a `run_scope(token, *, adopt=True)` context manager that sets and restores it. `adopt=True` (the default) means: if a token is ALREADY active, keep it and ignore the proposed one, so an inner scope joins the outer partition rather than splitting it — this is what keeps one `forge sprint` invocation, from entry-skipped intake through the last story, in a single partition even though the entry pass knows only `gate_run_id` and the sprint knows only `resolved.name`. `adopt=False` forces the given token and is used only where a worker thread re-enters a token it captured from its submitting thread (ContextVars do not cross ThreadPoolExecutor workers). The token value itself is `run_warning_key(state)` where a coordinator state exists — the same sprint-scoped key AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS uses — and `sprint_run_token(sprint_id_or_name)` (`f"sprint:{value}"`, matching run_warning_key's sprint form) where only a sprint identifier is in scope. Because of adoption, the two derivations never need to agree: whichever runs first wins for the whole invocation. `current_run_token()` returning None means "not inside a run": the quarantine neither records nor excludes, and behaviour is exactly today's.
(b) `ModelQuarantine` — a lock-guarded `dict[run_token, dict[dispatch_key, detail]]`. Every method takes the token explicitly: `record(token, key, detail)`, `contains(token, key)`, `snapshot(token)`, `overlay(token, availability)`, `discard(token)`. There is no reset-by-comparison and no single active key, so interleaved runs cannot clear or misattribute each other's evidence. Details are shaped like availability_detail() output (reason, auth mode, model/label, matched signal, checked_at) so format_unavailable_detail renders runtime and catalog exclusions identically. `overlay` returns a new StoryAvailability whose quarantined keys read `ModelAvailability(state=MODEL_AVAILABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, freshness current)` and whose other answers are unchanged; it never mutates its input, never restores an identity to available, and never writes to RETIRED_MODEL_REGISTRY, profiles or catalogs. Token partitions are bounded: `discard(token)` at the outermost scope exit, plus an LRU cap (16 partitions) so a long-lived process cannot accumulate. Module singleton `MODEL_QUARANTINE`, mirroring AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS at line 754. Export new names in __all__.
(c) `attempt_dispatch_key(profile, *, model_used=None, transport_used=None)` — the identity of one concrete attempt. Composes canonical_model_id(provider, model, kind) with transport.runner, provider and base_url exactly as dispatch_key() does, preferring model_used/transport_used when the attempt reported them. Because registration is now per attempt, `profile` is already the single-model profile that ran (the api_fallback profile, or run_api_agent's `current_profile` built at api.py:1187), so provider and base_url come from it directly and no fallback-spec reconstruction is needed — this is what makes a refused API fallback quarantine the *API* identity and leave its CLI primary eligible. Takes no ForgeConfig (runners have none); sound because profile_dispatch_key's only config use is the optional `identity` field, which dispatch_key does not read. Returns None rather than raising.
(d) `account_model_refusal(result, profile) -> QuarantineSignal | None` — an explicit, enumerated predicate over one attempt. Matches a small named table of known account/model-access refusal signatures (seeded with the Codex "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account" shape from the incident, over result.output and result.raw), and separately `failure_code == runner_codex.PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE` combined with the dispatched model string appearing in the refusal text. The signal names which rule matched. A pre-generation refusal matching no signature returns a distinct "unmatched" outcome carrying the raw reason, so an uncovered provider wording is visible in the run rather than silently non-quarantining. A bare 400 invalid_request_error with no model-access wording must not quarantine.
(e) `select_dispatchable(candidates, availability, config) -> DispatchSelection` — pure, no state: returns the first candidate whose overlaid answer is not unavailable, plus the list of excluded candidates with their reasons, or `None` with the full exclusion list when every candidate is gone. This is the single narrowing rule steps 4 and 5 both use; unverified stays eligible here exactly as everywhere else.

steps.description: Classify and register every attempt at the runner attempt seams
steps.details:
Add `_register_attempt(result, profile)` to each runner module (one shared implementation imported lazily from model_availability to avoid an import cycle): call account_model_refusal; on a match record attempt_dispatch_key under current_run_token() and log one `⚠ ROUTING  <label> quarantined — <reason> (<signal>)` line; on an unmatched pre-generation refusal log the raw reason with the signal absent. A None run token makes it a no-op. It returns the result unchanged, so it can be wrapped around existing expressions without restructuring control flow.
Instrumenting run_agent/run_api_agent here is what makes every caller covered by construction — including the two intake-remediation passes, whose dispatch is `_build_intake_agent_caller._call`'s plain run_agent call (sprint/runner.py:264). Those passes need no code of their own in this step; step 3 gives them a token.
Call sites, each holding a single-model attempt: - cli.py::run_agent — around each `_run_claude`/`_run_codex`/`_run_gemini`/`_run_ghaw`
  result, BEFORE `_maybe_run_api_fallback` runs, so a refused CLI primary is registered
  even when a later fallback succeeds and replaces the returned result.
- cli.py::run_agent — the direct API branch (line 649) registers nothing itself;
  registration for API attempts lives solely in api.py, so nothing double-registers.
- api.py::run_api_agent — inside the preference-list loop after `_run_single_api_model`
  (line 1189), against `current_profile`, for every iteration including non-final ones.
  This covers both the plain API path and every attempt made on behalf of
  `_maybe_run_api_fallback`, whose legacy api_fallback profile and each
  `_build_cli_fallback_api_profile` entry are dispatched through run_api_agent.

Result: several refused attempts followed by a final failure register all of them; a refused attempt followed by success registers the refused one only.
Also in cli.py: - POOL TOKEN PROPAGATION. ContextVars do not cross ThreadPoolExecutor workers. Capture
  `current_run_token()` in run_agent_pool before submitting and re-enter
  `run_scope(token, adopt=False)` inside `_timed_agent` (line 867), so reviewer-pool
  members register and honour the run's quarantine. This is also what closes the standing
  review-pool theme without touching review_pool.py: the primary reviewer dispatch is
  run_agent_pool, and both its singleton path (line 839) and its executor path (line 871)
  reach run_agent, which is now instrumented per attempt.
- BACKSTOP GUARD. At the top of run_agent, and again in `_maybe_run_api_fallback` before
  each fallback attempt, skip a dispatch whose identity is already quarantined under the
  current token, returning an unsuccessful AgentResult with cost_usd 0.0 and failure_code
  `model_unavailable_quarantined` without dispatching. This is explicitly a last-resort
  bound on repeat spend, NOT the mechanism for continuing on remaining models — step 5
  makes every fixed-role site choose a surviving candidate before it ever reaches here,
  and step 4 excludes routed phases at routing.

steps.description: Establish the run token at every run-owning entry, including both pre-story intake passes, without changing any signature
steps.details:
The scope is opened at the OUTERMOST run-owning boundary and adopted inward, so no sprint-owned dispatch can fall outside it.
- cli/sprint.py: open `run_scope(sprint_run_token(gate_run_id))` around the region that
  spans BOTH the entry-skipped remediation call (line 1419) and the subsequent run_sprint
  invocation, and `MODEL_QUARANTINE.discard(token)` on exit. This is the fix for the
  named P1 on the entry-skipped path: its dispatch is the same run_agent call step 2
  instruments, it simply had no token, so a live refusal during entry remediation was
  dropped and every later story met it again. Because the scope also encloses run_sprint,
  a refusal observed there excludes the identity for the stories that follow even though
  the entry pass knows only `gate_run_id` and never sees `resolved.name`.
- sprint/runner.py: wrap the run_sprint body in
  `run_scope(sprint_run_token(_ctx.resolved.name))`. Under `forge sprint` this ADOPTS the
  CLI token and is a no-op; for any other caller of run_sprint it establishes the sprint's
  own partition. Either way the in-run intake pass at line 6464 — which runs before batch
  preflight and before any story is submitted — is now inside a scope, which is the other
  half of the named P1.
- sprint/runner.py: at per-story submission, capture `current_run_token()` and re-enter
  `run_scope(token, adopt=False)` inside the worker thread, for the same
  ContextVar-does-not-cross-threads reason as run_agent_pool. Sibling stories of one
  sprint therefore share the partition by design.
- coordinator/engine.py: wrap the body of each run entry (run_task, run_from_dev,
  run_from_review, run_review_only) in `run_scope(run_warning_key(state))`. Inside a
  sprint this adopts the sprint token; a standalone `forge run` gets its own and discards
  it at exit.

No parameter is added to any of these functions, so callers outside this plan's files — the rest of src/theforge/cli/*, src/theforge/eval/preflight_harness.py, provider-readiness calls — are untouched; those that do not enter a run scope get a None token and behave exactly as today.

steps.description: Apply the quarantine to the availability answer routing already consumes
steps.details:
In story_availability_for (preflight.py:1289), keep memoizing the *raw* resolved StoryAvailability on state.model_availability and return `MODEL_QUARANTINE.overlay(current_run_token(), raw)` on every call including memo hits. Overlaying after the memo read is what makes a refusal recorded mid-story — or during intake, before the first story existed — visible at the next routing boundary; keeping the memo raw is what stops run-scoped state being cached as the account catalog's answer. Apply the same overlay to plan_flow.py's direct resolve_story_availability call at the post-plan checkpoint (near line 652) before model_availability and incumbent_availability are built.
Nothing downstream changes: _apply_static_availability, refuse_unroutable_phases, assign_models, pinned-pool member drop, the NoAvailableModelError stop and the AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS emit all consume the overlaid answer and already behave correctly for an unavailable identity — a quarantined pool member is dropped and the run proceeds (runbook:173-181), a quarantined singleton or pinned role goes through the shipped no-available-model stop (runbook:190-202).

steps.description: Every fixed-role selector filters its candidates through the overlaid answer
steps.details:
New module role_availability.py exposes `dispatchable_profile(config, state, candidates, *, role, log) -> DispatchSelection`: resolves the overlaid answer — via story_availability_for when a coordinator state exists (lazy import), and via resolve_story_availability(config) plus the same overlay when `state is None`, which is the pre-story case both intake passes are in — applies select_dispatchable, logs one `⚠ ROUTING  <role> <model> excluded — <reason>; using <chosen>` line on a reseat, and returns the selection with its exclusions. It never raises — each caller decides what an empty selection means, because the right outcome differs by role.
- preflight_flow.py: `_availability_checked_preflight_profile` (line 390) is rewritten to
  call the shared helper over preflight_dispatch_profiles(config), preserving its current
  behaviour exactly — reseat onto the configured fallback, raise NoAvailableModelError
  when neither is invocable — so the two derivations cannot drift apart again.
- preflight_decomposition_flow.py: `generate_decomposition_assessment` (line 245) passes
  the same preflight candidate list through the helper before seal_assessment_profile,
  and on an empty selection returns its existing `_unavailable(...)` with the exclusion
  reasons. It must NOT raise: the assessment happens after preflight is paid and is
  optional. This is the concrete path the prior reviews named — a preflight primary that
  reseated onto its fallback no longer has the original primary re-dispatched here.
- escalation_advisor_flow.py: `_select_advisor_profile` (line 108) narrows
  `phase_eligible`/`capable` by the overlaid answer alongside the existing capability
  exclusion, so a reviewer identity refused minutes earlier is not the advisor's choice;
  an emptied pool raises the existing ValueError/NoCapableCandidateError, which
  run_escalation_advisor already renders as `advisor unavailable` and continues the run.
- knowledge_summary_flow.py: `_summary_profile` (line 360) already returns
  `(profile, reason)`; return `(None, reason)` when the resolved summary profile — the
  API-transport one `_project_summary_api_profile` actually dispatches — is unavailable,
  reusing the module's documented "no dispatchable profile" outcome.
- workspace.py: `_resolve_merge_conflicts` (dispatch at line 340) checks config.dev_profile
  before dispatching and, when unavailable, skips the agent resolution and returns the
  existing unresolved-conflict outcome naming the exclusion, rather than paying for a
  certain refusal during landing.
- sprint/runner.py: `_build_intake_agent_caller` (line 251) runs the remediation profile
  it derives from config.dev_profile through the helper with `state=None`, immediately
  after its existing check_agent_auth call and in exactly the same shape: an unavailable
  profile returns `(None, detail)` naming the exclusion, which the pass already renders as
  `auto-fix enabled but no intake agent caller is available: <reason>` and proceeds
  without dispatching. Because both passes — in-run (line 6464) and entry-skipped, via
  entry_intake.remediate_entry_skipped_issues — go through this one builder, one edit
  covers both; and because both now run inside a token scope (step 3), a refusal either
  one *does* meet is registered for the stories that follow.

Each site is one helper call plus one branch into a failure path the site already has, so no new terminal state is introduced anywhere.

steps.description: Surface the quarantine in the audit and document it
steps.details: Record `MODEL_QUARANTINE.snapshot(token)` on the run's audit alongside the existing availability evidence, so the cross-phase value that changed routing — which signal matched, or that a refusal went unmatched — is inspectable after the fact. Extend the "Model availability gate (issue #2950)" section with a live-quarantine subsection: an explicit refusal outranks any prior state including unverified; it is scoped to one `forge sprint` invocation, starting at entry-skipped intake remediation and ending with the last story (shared by sibling stories, never across sprints, never persisted, gone on a re-exec); it is keyed on the identity of the attempt that actually refused, so a refused API fallback does not disable its CLI primary and a refused CLI primary is recorded even when its fallback then succeeds; the fixed-role dispatches (intake remediation, decomposition assessment, escalation advisor, knowledge summary, landing conflict resolution) filter their configured candidates the same way preflight does; and an unrecognised refusal wording appears in the log as unmatched and falls back to today's per-story behaviour. Note the ordering explicitly against runbook:329, which already places the readiness gate ahead of intake remediation and batch preflight.

steps.description: Tests at the attempt seams, the run-token boundary, both intake passes, and every fixed role
steps.details:
Predicate and key (unit): the Codex ChatGPT-account refusal matches and names its signal; a bare 400 invalid_request_error does not quarantine and reports unmatched.
ATTEMPT SEAMS (the P1 the terminal-seam design failed): - a CLI refusal followed by a *successful* API fallback — assert the CLI primary identity
  is quarantined and excluded later, and the successful fallback identity stays eligible;
- an API preference-list primary refused and a later entry succeeding (api.py loop) —
  same two assertions;
- a refused api_fallback behind a healthy CLI primary — the fallback identity is
  excluded while the primary remains eligible, and another profile naming that refused
  fallback model is excluded (the cross-transport case both prior attempts failed).

INTAKE PASSES (the named P1, one test per path, both asserting a LIVE refusal — the identity is available or unverified at resolution time and only the dispatch refuses, so step 5's pre-dispatch filter cannot be what produces the pass): - in-run: an intake remediation dispatch under run_sprint is refused; assert the identity
  is recorded under the sprint token and that a story submitted afterwards excludes it at
  routing and never dispatches it;
- entry-skipped: remediate_entry_skipped_issues is refused inside the CLI scope; assert
  the same identity is excluded by the run_sprint stories that follow in the same
  invocation, proving token adoption across `gate_run_id` and `resolved.name`;
- and the step 5 companion: an intake profile already known unavailable yields the
  existing `no intake agent caller is available` detail with the exclusion reason and no
  dispatch at all.

RUN TOKEN: two distinct tokens active concurrently do not see each other's entries and neither clears the other; `run_scope` nested inside an active scope adopts rather than partitions; a run_agent call with no token records and excludes nothing; a standalone runner invocation after a completed sprint inherits nothing; a refusal recorded in story A of a sprint excludes the identity in story B of the same sprint; a second sprint in the same process starts clean. Parallel case: record a refusal from one worker while others are in flight and assert every later routing read sees it (this is the interleaving test the prior plan only reasoned about).
OVERLAY (routing): quarantined previously-available and previously-unverified identities are both excluded by assign_models and refuse_unroutable_phases; an unverified identity with no refusal stays eligible and warns once; a raw availability memo created before a refusal reflects it at the next routing boundary; a phase emptied by quarantine raises the existing NoAvailableModelError before further dispatch; a retired-catalog entry stays non-routable regardless.
FIXED ROLES (new file): an unavailable preflight primary reseats preflight AND the subsequent decomposition assessment onto the same fallback (the named regression); a reviewer refusal excludes that identity from the escalation advisor's selection and the advisor still runs on a remaining candidate; an unavailable summary profile skips the summary with a reason instead of dispatching; an unavailable dev profile skips agent merge-conflict resolution. Each asserts no dispatch occurred, not merely that the call failed.
CHOKEPOINT: drive run_agent through the existing fake-CLI subprocess pattern in test_runner_codex.py to prove a refused dispatch records the quarantine and a second call on the same profile returns the non-dispatching model_unavailable_quarantined result with cost 0.0 rather than spawning the CLI. Pool coverage rides on the same instrumentation via run_agent_pool, with one test asserting a refusal by a pool member under the executor path is registered under the submitting thread's token.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Three states; available routes, unavailable is excluded and logged, unverified stays fully eligible with a once-per-run warning.

This plan adds only the missing clause: an explicit provider refusal converts an identity to unavailable for the rest of the run.
Two seams, no threading. (1) Registration goes at runners/cli.py::run_agent's single return seam, which every generative dispatch in the codebase passes through — including the sites prior reviews flagged as missed — and which is the only point that knows the identity that actually refused (model_used/transport_used after api_fallback). (2) Consumption goes into the existing #2950 availability answer via an overlay applied at story_availability_for and the post-plan checkpoint, so routing exclusion, pinned-pool member drop, the stop path, warnings and audit all reuse shipped machinery unchanged. Run scoping copies the AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS pattern: a module singleton keyed on run_warning_key(state), reset by key comparison, not a parameter threaded through engine/sprint/state. review_pool.py, engine.py, state.py, run_setup.py and sprint/collision.py are deliberately not modified.

steps.description: Run-scoped quarantine, resolved-identity key, and refusal predicate
steps.details:
Add three things beside the existing availability code.
(a) `resolved_dispatch_key(profile, *, model_used, transport_used, api_fallback)` — builds a dispatch_key from the identity that *actually ran*, not the configured one. Composes canonical_model_id(provider, model, kind) with transport.runner, provider and base_url exactly as dispatch_key() does, substituting model_used for profile.model and transport_used for transport.kind when present, and taking provider/base_url from the applicable api_fallback spec when transport_used == "api" on a cli profile. Falls back to the configured profile's identity only when the resolved fields are absent. Takes no ForgeConfig (run_agent has none); the config-free path is sound because profile_dispatch_key's only config use is the optional `identity` field, which dispatch_key does not read. Returns None rather than raising.
(b) `ModelQuarantine` — a lock-guarded store of dispatch key -> detail dict, shaped like availability_detail() output (reason, auth mode, model/label, checked_at) so format_unavailable_detail renders runtime and catalog exclusions identically. Public surface: `reset(run_key)` (clears only when run_key differs from the stored one, so it is idempotent per story, exactly like AvailabilityWarnings.pending), `record(key, detail)`, `contains(key)`, `snapshot()`, and `overlay(availability) -> StoryAvailability` returning a new StoryAvailability whose quarantined keys read ModelAvailability(state=MODEL_AVAILABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, freshness current) and whose other answers are unchanged. Never mutates its input and never writes to RETIRED_MODEL_REGISTRY, profiles or catalogs — run-scoped only. Module singleton `MODEL_QUARANTINE`, mirroring AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS at line 754. Export the new names in __all__.
(c) `account_model_refusal(result, profile) -> QuarantineSignal | None` — an explicit, enumerated predicate. It matches on a small named table of known account/model-access refusal signatures (seeded with the Codex "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account" shape from the incident, over result.output and result.raw), and separately on failure_code == runner_codex.PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE combined with the dispatched model string appearing in the refusal text. The returned signal names *which* rule matched. Crucially it also reports a miss explicitly: a pre-generation refusal that matched no signature returns a distinct "unmatched" outcome carrying the raw reason, so a provider whose wording is not yet covered is visible in the run rather than silently non-quarantining. A bare 400 invalid_request_error with no model-access wording must not quarantine.

steps.description: Register refusals and refuse repeats at the single dispatch chokepoint
steps.details:
In run_agent, after the result passes through _fill_invocation_identity / _stamp_configured_identity (so model_used and transport_used already describe the api_fallback attempt when one ran), call account_model_refusal. On a match, compute resolved_dispatch_key from the result's resolved identity and record it in MODEL_QUARANTINE with the matched-signal name, the refusal reason, the auth mode and the timestamp, and log one `⚠ ROUTING  <label> quarantined — <reason>` line. On an unmatched pre-generation refusal, log the raw reason with the matched-signal absent, so an unrecognised wording is operator-visible. This one seam covers every generative dispatch — preflight, plan and plan review, dev, review pool (run_agent_pool calls run_agent per member, including the singleton path), decomposition assessment, escalation advisor, knowledge summary and landing merge-conflict resolution — without any of those modules being touched or a quarantine being threaded to them.
Add the repeat guard at the top of run_agent: if MODEL_QUARANTINE.contains the configured profile's identity, return an unsuccessful AgentResult with cost_usd 0.0 and a `model_unavailable_quarantined` failure_code *without dispatching*. Add the same one-line check in _maybe_run_api_fallback against the fallback profile's identity so a quarantined fallback is not re-attempted either. Routed phases normally never reach this guard — step 3's overlay excludes them at routing — so its purpose is the fixed-profile sites that consult no routing at all: they stop paying for the identical refusal once per story. Import model_availability lazily inside the functions to avoid an import cycle with the runners package.

steps.description: Apply the quarantine to the availability answer routing already consumes
steps.details:
In story_availability_for (preflight.py:1289), call MODEL_QUARANTINE.reset(run_warning_key(state)) — idempotent, clears only on a new run — then keep memoizing the *raw* resolved StoryAvailability on state.model_availability and return MODEL_QUARANTINE.overlay(raw) on every call including memo hits. Overlaying after the memo read is what makes a refusal recorded mid-story visible to the next routing boundary, and keeping the memo raw is what stops a run-scoped overlay being cached as the account catalog's answer. Apply the same overlay to plan_flow.py's direct resolve_story_availability call at the post-plan checkpoint (near line 652) before model_availability and incumbent_availability are built. In sprint/runner.py:5361, add MODEL_QUARANTINE.reset beside the existing AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS.reset so a second sprint in one process starts clean.
Nothing downstream changes: _apply_static_availability, refuse_unroutable_phases, assign_models, pinned-pool member drop, the NoAvailableModelError stop and the AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS emit all consume the overlaid answer and already behave correctly for an unavailable identity. That is also what resolves the singleton-vs-pool question the prior review raised — a quarantined pool member is dropped and the run proceeds, a quarantined singleton or pinned role goes through the shipped no-available-model stop — without this plan restating either behaviour.

Extend the "Model availability gate (issue #2950)" section with a subsection for the live quarantine: an explicit refusal outranks any prior state including unverified, it is scoped to the run and never persisted, it is keyed on the identity that actually refused (so a refused API fallback does not disable its CLI primary), and an unrecognised refusal wording appears in the log as unmatched and falls back to today's per-story behaviour.

steps.description: Tests at the two seams and the identity boundary
steps.details:
Predicate and key (unit): the Codex ChatGPT-account refusal matches and names its signal; a bare 400 invalid_request_error does not quarantine and reports unmatched; a refusal returned with model_used/transport_used describing an api_fallback quarantines the fallback identity and leaves the cli primary's identity eligible, while a different profile naming that refused fallback model is excluded — the cross-transport case both prior attempts failed.
Overlay (routing): a quarantined previously-available identity and a quarantined previously-unverified identity are both excluded by assign_models and refuse_unroutable_phases; an unverified identity with no refusal stays eligible and warns once; a raw availability memo created *before* a refusal reflects it at the next routing boundary; a phase emptied by quarantine raises the existing NoAvailableModelError before any further dispatch; a retired-catalog entry stays non-routable regardless.
Run seam: a refusal recorded during one story prevents a later story in the same sprint from routing to that identity, and the quarantine is cleared for a second sprint in the same process. Since parallel sprint stories share the singleton, have the parallel case record a refusal from one worker while others are in flight and assert every later routing read sees it.

plan.approach:
Everything in the acceptance criteria except the live-refusal quarantine shipped under #2950 (three states, per-account/auth-mode dispatch identities, no-available-model stop, non-generative resolution, retired-catalog convergence, timestamped answers — docs/guides/controller-runbook.md:92-208). This plan adds the missing clause: an explicit provider refusal converts an identity to unavailable for the rest of the run, and every dispatch site — routed or fixed-role — consults that answer.
Three corrections to the prior attempt, each answering a recurring P1.
(1) REGISTRATION IS PER ATTEMPT, NOT PER RETURNED RESULT. run_agent's return value is not the set of attempts: runners/cli.py::_maybe_run_api_fallback consumes a refused CLI result and may return a later successful API result, and runners/api.py::run_api_agent's preference loop (line 1184) discards every failed model before the one that succeeds. So classification happens where a concrete single-model attempt result exists — beside each `_run_*` CLI call in run_agent, and inside run_api_agent's per-model loop on `current_profile`. Every attempt is classified before any fallback loop advances, so a refused primary followed by a successful fallback quarantines the primary and leaves the fallback eligible.
(2) THE QUARANTINE IS PARTITIONED BY AN EXPLICIT RUN TOKEN, carried ambiently in a contextvars.ContextVar rather than threaded through signatures. reset()-with-one-active-key is abandoned: interleaved runs corrupted it and run_agent had no run identity to attribute a refusal to. The coordinator sets the token at run entry; runners read it. No signature in engine.py/sprint changes, so cli/*, eval/preflight_harness.py and every other external caller keep working — and, absent a token, the quarantine is inert in both directions, so a standalone runner invocation after a completed sprint inherits nothing.
(3) FIXED-ROLE SELECTORS CONSUME THE AVAILABILITY ANSWER. A generic run_agent guard can only fail a dispatch; it cannot choose the remaining model, which is what the criteria require. The five roles that select a profile from configuration rather than from routing — decomposition assessment, escalation advisor, knowledge summary, landing merge-conflict resolution, sprint intake remediation — each filter their own candidates through one shared helper before dispatching, exactly as preflight_flow._availability_checked_preflight_profile already does. The run_agent guard remains, demoted to a last-resort backstop.
Routing-side consumption is unchanged from the prior plan: an overlay on the #2950 answer at story_availability_for and the post-plan checkpoint, so exclusion, pinned-pool member drop, the stop path, warnings and audit all reuse shipped machinery.

steps.description: Run-token-partitioned quarantine, attempt-identity key, refusal predicate, shared selector
steps.details:
Four additions beside the existing availability code.
(a) RUN TOKEN. `RUN_TOKEN: ContextVar[str | None]`, plus `current_run_token()` and a `run_scope(token)` context manager that sets and restores it. The token is `run_warning_key(state)` — the same sprint-scoped key AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS uses, so sibling stories of one parallel sprint deliberately share one quarantine (a refusal one worker observes must exclude the model for the others) while two sprints, or a sprint and a later standalone call, never share. `current_run_token()` returning None means "not inside a run": the quarantine neither records nor excludes, and behaviour is exactly today's.
(b) `ModelQuarantine` — a lock-guarded `dict[run_token, dict[dispatch_key, detail]]`. Every method takes the token explicitly: `record(token, key, detail)`, `contains(token, key)`, `snapshot(token)`, `overlay(token, availability)`, `discard(token)`. There is no reset-by-comparison and no single active key, so interleaved runs cannot clear or misattribute each other's evidence. Details are shaped like availability_detail() output (reason, auth mode, model/label, matched signal, checked_at) so format_unavailable_detail renders runtime and catalog exclusions identically. `overlay` returns a new StoryAvailability whose quarantined keys read `ModelAvailability(state=MODEL_AVAILABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, freshness current)` and whose other answers are unchanged; it never mutates its input, never restores an identity to available, and never writes to RETIRED_MODEL_REGISTRY, profiles or catalogs. Token partitions are bounded: `discard(token)` at sprint/run exit, plus an LRU cap (16 partitions) so a long-lived process cannot accumulate. Module singleton `MODEL_QUARANTINE`, mirroring AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS at line 754. Export new names in __all__.
(c) `attempt_dispatch_key(profile, *, model_used=None, transport_used=None)` — the identity of one concrete attempt. Composes canonical_model_id(provider, model, kind) with transport.runner, provider and base_url exactly as dispatch_key() does, preferring model_used/transport_used when the attempt reported them. Because registration is now per attempt, `profile` is already the single-model profile that ran (the api_fallback profile, or run_api_agent's `current_profile` built at api.py:1187), so provider and base_url come from it directly and no fallback-spec reconstruction is needed — this is what makes a refused API fallback quarantine the *API* identity and leave its CLI primary eligible. Takes no ForgeConfig (runners have none); sound because profile_dispatch_key's only config use is the optional `identity` field, which dispatch_key does not read. Returns None rather than raising.
(d) `account_model_refusal(result, profile) -> QuarantineSignal | None` — an explicit, enumerated predicate over one attempt. Matches a small named table of known account/model-access refusal signatures (seeded with the Codex "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account" shape from the incident, over result.output and result.raw), and separately `failure_code == runner_codex.PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE` combined with the dispatched model string appearing in the refusal text. The signal names which rule matched. A pre-generation refusal matching no signature returns a distinct "unmatched" outcome carrying the raw reason, so an uncovered provider wording is visible in the run rather than silently non-quarantining. A bare 400 invalid_request_error with no model-access wording must not quarantine.
(e) `select_dispatchable(candidates, availability, config) -> DispatchSelection` — pure, no state: returns the first candidate whose overlaid answer is not unavailable, plus the list of excluded candidates with their reasons, or `None` with the full exclusion list when every candidate is gone. This is the single narrowing rule steps 4 and 5 both use; unverified stays eligible here exactly as everywhere else.

steps.description: Classify and register every attempt at the runner attempt seams
steps.details:
Add `_register_attempt(result, profile)` to each runner module (one shared implementation imported lazily from model_availability to avoid an import cycle): call account_model_refusal; on a match record attempt_dispatch_key under current_run_token() and log one `⚠ ROUTING  <label> quarantined — <reason> (<signal>)` line; on an unmatched pre-generation refusal log the raw reason with the signal absent. A None run token makes it a no-op. It returns the result unchanged, so it can be wrapped around existing expressions without restructuring control flow.
Call sites, each holding a single-model attempt: - cli.py::run_agent — around each `_run_claude`/`_run_codex`/`_run_gemini`/`_run_ghaw`
  result, BEFORE `_maybe_run_api_fallback` runs, so a refused CLI primary is registered
  even when a later fallback succeeds and replaces the returned result.
- cli.py::run_agent — the direct API branch (line 649) registers its own attempt only
  if run_api_agent did not (see below); to avoid double-registration, registration for
  API attempts lives solely in api.py and run_agent's API branch adds nothing.
- api.py::run_api_agent — inside the preference-list loop after `_run_single_api_model`
  (line 1189), against `current_profile`, for every iteration including non-final ones.
  This covers both the plain API path and every attempt made on behalf of
  `_maybe_run_api_fallback`, whose legacy api_fallback profile and each
  `_build_cli_fallback_api_profile` entry are dispatched through run_api_agent.

Result: several refused attempts followed by a final failure register all of them; a refused attempt followed by success registers the refused one only.
Also in cli.py: - POOL TOKEN PROPAGATION. ContextVars do not cross ThreadPoolExecutor workers. Capture
  `current_run_token()` in run_agent_pool before submitting and re-enter `run_scope` for
  it inside `_timed_agent` (line 867), so reviewer-pool members register and honour the
  run's quarantine. This is also what closes the standing review-pool theme without
  touching review_pool.py: the primary reviewer dispatch is run_agent_pool, and both its
  singleton path (line 839) and its executor path (line 871) reach run_agent, which is
  now instrumented per attempt.
- BACKSTOP GUARD. At the top of run_agent, and again in `_maybe_run_api_fallback` before
  each fallback attempt, skip a dispatch whose identity is already quarantined under the
  current token, returning an unsuccessful AgentResult with cost_usd 0.0 and failure_code
  `model_unavailable_quarantined` without dispatching. This is explicitly a last-resort
  bound on repeat spend, NOT the mechanism for continuing on remaining models — step 5
  makes every fixed-role site choose a surviving candidate before it ever reaches here,
  and step 4 excludes routed phases at routing.

steps.description: Establish the run token at run entry, without changing any signature
steps.details:
Wrap the body of each coordinator run entry (run_task, run_from_dev, run_from_review, run_review_only) in `run_scope(run_warning_key(state))`, and the sprint's per-story submission likewise, so every dispatch made under a run — in whatever thread the story runs on — sees its own token. Because each sprint worker enters the coordinator itself, the token is set inside the worker thread and no cross-thread propagation is needed beyond run_agent_pool's (step 2).
No parameter is added to any of these functions, so callers outside this plan's files — src/theforge/cli/*, src/theforge/eval/preflight_harness.py, provider-readiness calls — are untouched; those that do not enter a run scope get a None token and behave exactly as today. At sprint completion call `MODEL_QUARANTINE.discard(token)`.

steps.description: Apply the quarantine to the availability answer routing already consumes
steps.details:
In story_availability_for (preflight.py:1289), keep memoizing the *raw* resolved StoryAvailability on state.model_availability and return `MODEL_QUARANTINE.overlay(current_run_token(), raw)` on every call including memo hits. Overlaying after the memo read is what makes a refusal recorded mid-story visible at the next routing boundary; keeping the memo raw is what stops run-scoped state being cached as the account catalog's answer. Apply the same overlay to plan_flow.py's direct resolve_story_availability call at the post-plan checkpoint (near line 652) before model_availability and incumbent_availability are built.
Nothing downstream changes: _apply_static_availability, refuse_unroutable_phases, assign_models, pinned-pool member drop, the NoAvailableModelError stop and the AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS emit all consume the overlaid answer and already behave correctly for an unavailable identity — a quarantined pool member is dropped and the run proceeds (runbook:173-181), a quarantined singleton or pinned role goes through the shipped no-available-model stop (runbook:190-202).

steps.description: Every fixed-role selector filters its candidates through the overlaid answer
steps.details:
New module role_availability.py exposes `dispatchable_profile(config, state, candidates, *, role, log) -> DispatchSelection`: reads the overlaid answer via story_availability_for (lazy import), applies select_dispatchable, logs one `⚠ ROUTING  <role> <model> excluded — <reason>; using <chosen>` line on a reseat, and returns the selection with its exclusions. It never raises — each caller decides what an empty selection means, because the right outcome differs by role.
- preflight_flow.py: `_availability_checked_preflight_profile` (line 390) is rewritten to
  call the shared helper over preflight_dispatch_profiles(config), preserving its current
  behaviour exactly — reseat onto the configured fallback, raise NoAvailableModelError
  when neither is invocable — so the two derivations cannot drift apart again.
- preflight_decomposition_flow.py: `generate_decomposition_assessment` (line 245) passes
  the same preflight candidate list through the helper before seal_assessment_profile,
  and on an empty selection returns its existing `_unavailable(...)` with the exclusion
  reasons. It must NOT raise: the assessment happens after preflight is paid and is
  optional. This is the concrete path the prior reviews named — a preflight primary that
  reseated onto its fallback no longer has the original primary re-dispatched here.
- escalation_advisor_flow.py: `_select_advisor_profile` (line 108) narrows
  `phase_eligible`/`capable` by the overlaid answer alongside the existing capability
  exclusion, so a reviewer identity refused minutes earlier is not the advisor's choice;
  an emptied pool raises the existing ValueError/NoCapableCandidateError, which
  run_escalation_advisor already renders as `advisor unavailable` and continues the run.
- knowledge_summary_flow.py: `_summary_profile` (line 360) already returns
  `(profile, reason)`; return `(None, reason)` when the resolved summary profile — the
  API-transport one `_project_summary_api_profile` actually dispatches — is unavailable,
  reusing the module's documented "no dispatchable profile" outcome.
- workspace.py: `_resolve_merge_conflicts` (dispatch at line 340) checks config.dev_profile
  before dispatching and, when unavailable, skips the agent resolution and returns the
  existing unresolved-conflict outcome naming the exclusion, rather than paying for a
  certain refusal during landing.
- sprint/runner.py: the intake-remediation dispatch (line 277) checks its profile the same
  way and skips remediation with the exclusion reason.

Each site is one helper call plus one branch into a failure path the site already has, so no new terminal state is introduced anywhere.

steps.description: Surface the quarantine in the audit and document it
steps.details: Record `MODEL_QUARANTINE.snapshot(token)` on the run's audit alongside the existing availability evidence, so the cross-phase value that changed routing — which signal matched, or that a refusal went unmatched — is inspectable after the fact. Extend the "Model availability gate (issue #2950)" section with a live-quarantine subsection: an explicit refusal outranks any prior state including unverified; it is scoped to the run (shared by sibling stories of one sprint, never across sprints, never persisted); it is keyed on the identity of the attempt that actually refused, so a refused API fallback does not disable its CLI primary and a refused CLI primary is recorded even when its fallback then succeeds; the fixed-role dispatches (decomposition assessment, escalation advisor, knowledge summary, landing conflict resolution, intake remediation) filter their configured candidates the same way preflight does; and an unrecognised refusal wording appears in the log as unmatched and falls back to today's per-story behaviour.

steps.description: Tests at the attempt seams, the run-token boundary, and every fixed role
steps.details:
Predicate and key (unit): the Codex ChatGPT-account refusal matches and names its signal; a bare 400 invalid_request_error does not quarantine and reports unmatched.
ATTEMPT SEAMS (the P1 the terminal-seam design failed): - a CLI refusal followed by a *successful* API fallback — assert the CLI primary identity
  is quarantined and excluded later, and the successful fallback identity stays eligible;
- an API preference-list primary refused and a later entry succeeding (api.py loop) —
  same two assertions;
- a refused api_fallback behind a healthy CLI primary — the fallback identity is
  excluded while the primary remains eligible, and another profile naming that refused
  fallback model is excluded (the cross-transport case both prior attempts failed).

RUN TOKEN: two distinct tokens active concurrently do not see each other's entries and neither clears the other; a run_agent call with no token records and excludes nothing; a standalone runner invocation after a completed sprint inherits nothing; a refusal recorded in story A of a sprint excludes the identity in story B of the same sprint; a second sprint in the same process starts clean. Parallel case: record a refusal from one worker while others are in flight and assert every later routing read sees it (this is the interleaving test the prior plan only reasoned about).
OVERLAY (routing): quarantined previously-available and previously-unverified identities are both excluded by assign_models and refuse_unroutable_phases; an unverified identity with no refusal stays eligible and warns once; a raw availability memo created before a refusal reflects it at the next routing boundary; a phase emptied by quarantine raises the existing NoAvailableModelError before further dispatch; a retired-catalog entry stays non-routable regardless.
FIXED ROLES (new file): an unavailable preflight primary reseats preflight AND the subsequent decomposition assessment onto the same fallback (the named regression); a reviewer refusal excludes that identity from the escalation advisor's selection and the advisor still runs on a remaining candidate; an unavailable summary profile skips the summary with a reason instead of dispatching; an unavailable dev profile skips agent merge-conflict resolution; an unavailable intake-remediation profile skips remediation. Each asserts no dispatch occurred, not merely that the call failed.
CHOKEPOINT: drive run_agent through the existing fake-CLI subprocess pattern in test_runner_codex.py to prove a refused dispatch records the quarantine and a second call on the same profile returns the non-dispatching model_unavailable_quarantined result with cost 0.0 rather than spawning the CLI. Pool coverage rides on the same instrumentation via run_agent_pool, with one test asserting a refusal by a pool member under the executor path is registered under the submitting thread's token.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Three states; available routes, unavailable is excluded and logged, unverified stays fully eligible with a once-per-run warning.
criteria_mapping.note: Shipped in #2950; step 4 changes only what the answer is overlaid with, step 7 re-asserts unverified-stays-eligible.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Availability resolved for the account and auth mode the run dispatches with; no fixed identifier status.
criteria_mapping.note: The quarantine is keyed on the identity of the attempt that refused, including transport, and is run-token-scoped state never written back to a catalog or profile.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A phase with nothing left stops the run before spend, naming exclusions and why.
criteria_mapping.note: Routed phases via the shipped stop; fixed roles via their own documented no-dispatchable-profile outcomes, each naming the exclusions.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Resolution needs no generative request and no operator action.
criteria_mapping.note: The quarantine adds evidence only from dispatches the run was already making.

criteria_mapping.criterion: An explicit refusal quarantines that model for the rest of the run, converts unverified to unavailable, and the run continues on the remaining models.
criteria_mapping.note: 'Continues on the remaining models' is step 5's job at fixed-role sites and step 4's at routed ones; step 2's guard only bounds repeat spend.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Hand-marked withdrawn catalog entries stay non-routable; sources converge toward unavailable, never toward available.
criteria_mapping.note: overlay() only ever forces unavailable; it cannot restore an identity to available.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Answers carry the time obtained; stale answers refreshed or reported stale.

risks.description: The run token is ambient (ContextVar), so a dispatch made in a thread the coordinator did not spawn would see no token and skip the quarantine.
risks.mitigation: The two thread boundaries in play are covered explicitly: sprint workers enter the coordinator and set their own token, run_agent_pool re-enters the scope inside each worker. A missed boundary degrades to today's behaviour — one repeated refusal — never to a wrong exclusion, and the fixed-role selectors of step 5 read availability on the coordinator thread regardless.

risks.description: Only the Codex refusal wording is known concretely, so another provider's refusal may not match.
risks.mitigation: The predicate reports unmatched pre-generation refusals explicitly in the log and audit with the raw reason, so a gap is visible rather than silent, and a miss fails open to today's behaviour.

risks.description: Registering per attempt means the classifier runs on every runner result, including successes.
risks.mitigation: It is a cheap early-out on result.success and failure_code before any string scanning, and it returns its input unchanged, so no control flow in either runner changes.

risks.description: Sibling stories of one parallel sprint share a token by design, so one story's refusal changes another's routing mid-flight.
risks.mitigation: That is the intended reading of 'no later story routes to it' and matches the shipped AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS scope. Records are under one lock and overlays read fresh snapshots, so interleaving order is the only nondeterminism; every interleaving either excludes or does not yet exclude, and neither is unsafe.

risks.description: run_agent and run_api_agent are used by eval and CLI entry points outside a coordinator run.
risks.mitigation: No signature changes, and with no ambient token the quarantine neither records nor excludes, so those callers behave exactly as today.
